How a commission is made.

Four stages, and you are part of all of them. Most commissions take three to eight weeks depending on the stone and the setting.

01

Consultation

Sit with a jeweller, not a salesperson. We discuss the occasion, your budget, the metal and the stone — and whether the idea in your head is the right one.

02

Sketch & quote

Hand drawings of the piece, and a written estimate that itemises metal, stones and making. Nothing is fixed until you approve the quote.

03

Hand crafting

Our karigars raise, engrave, set and polish the piece in stages. You are welcome at the bench for any of them, and we send photographs as it progresses.

04

Assay & handover

Independent hallmarking and certification where needed, a final weigh-in, and the piece handed over with its paperwork and a service file.

What to bring

A commission goes faster when you bring anything you already love.

  • A sketch, a photograph, or a screenshot — anything that shows the shape you mean.
  • A piece you already own that fits the way you want, for sizing and weight.
  • Old gold you would like remade, exchanged or valued. Bring the paperwork if you have it.
  • Your dates. If it is for a wedding, tell us the wedding date first, not last.

Start with a conversation.

No deposit, no obligation, and no pressure to decide on the day.
